scenes.visual: Title card 'Harvey's Arithmetic' over an old-paper texture with a quill and a cartoon heart. Same COLOUR MAP as the first film: oxygen-poor blood BLUE; oxygen-rich blood RED; ventricle drawn as a GOLD cup or lift; vessels GREY. All drawings are cartoons labelled 'schematic'. No molecules.

scenes.tts: The first film compared two circuits carrying the same flow. How big is that flow, and what did measuring it first prove?
scenes.visual: A brief recap thumbnail of the first film's landscape: two GOLD lifts, equal flow counters ticking. The counters zoom up to fill the screen, then fade into an old-paper page.
scenes.narration: The first film compared two circuits carrying the same flow. How big is that flow, and what did measuring it first prove?

scenes.tts: For centuries, the standard account came from Galen. Blood was made continually from food in the liver. The tissues it reached used it up.
scenes.caption: For centuries, the standard account came from Galen. Blood was made continually from food in the liver. The tissues it reached used it up.
scenes.visual: On-screen date 'until 1628'. A cartoon body: a bread icon enters the gut, a liver (brown block, labelled 'liver') emits RED drops, which drift out to the limbs and vanish with small puffs. Label 'Galen: made from food, used up'.
scenes.narration: For centuries, the standard account came from Galen. Blood was made continually from food in the liver. The tissues it reached used it up.

scenes.tts: William Harvey, a London physician, tested this on the human arm. He tied a band round the upper arm. Tied tight, it stopped the pulse below it.
scenes.visual: A cartoon forearm with GREY arteries deep and GREY-BLUE veins near the surface. A band tightens on the upper arm; a pulse-wave icon at the wrist flattens, and the surface veins stay flat. Label 'tight band: no pulse, veins flat'.
scenes.narration: William Harvey, a London physician, tested this on the human arm. He tied a band round the upper arm. Tied tight, it stopped the pulse below it.

scenes.tts: Tied more loosely, it let the arteries drive blood in, but stopped its return. The veins below the band swelled. So blood enters a limb by arteries, and leaves by veins.
scenes.visual: The band loosens a little. The wrist pulse icon returns. RED dots flow down the deep arteries into the hand; BLUE dots back up in the surface veins below the band, which visibly swell. Arrows: 'in by arteries', 'out by veins'.
scenes.narration: Tied more loosely, it let the arteries drive blood in, but stopped its return. The veins below the band swelled. So blood enters a limb by arteries, and leaves by veins.

scenes.tts: Then Harvey asked a question of quantity. He made small guesses, on purpose, for how much blood leaves the heart at each beat.
scenes.visual: The GOLD ventricle cup from the first film ejects a small scoop of RED blood each beat. The scoop is visibly undersized, with a tag 'deliberately low guess'. A metronome ticks beside it.
scenes.narration: Then Harvey asked a question of quantity. He made small guesses, on purpose, for how much blood leaves the heart at each beat.

scenes.tts: He multiplied by the number of beats in half an hour. Even that low product was more blood than the whole body contains, and far more than food could replace.
scenes.visual: Each scoop drops into a tall glass tank. Beside the tank stands a body silhouette filled with RED, labelled 'all the blood in the body' (on screen only: '5 L'). A clock face sweeps through half an hour. The tank level passes the silhouette's level, then passes it again and again, overflowing. A small bread icon next to it stays tiny.
scenes.narration: He multiplied by the number of beats in half an hour. Even that low product was more blood than the whole body contains, and far more than food could replace.

scenes.tts: Now test the argument. Suppose his guess per beat was still too big, by a full half. Does his conclusion fall?
scenes.visual: The scoop shrinks to half its size, labelled 'scoop halved'. The tank empties and the clock resets to zero. Two answer cards: 'conclusion falls', 'conclusion stands'.
scenes.narration: Now test the argument. Suppose his guess per beat was still too big, by a full half. Does his conclusion fall?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Cards hold. A 5-second ring timer counts down at bottom right.

scenes.tts: It stands. Even with half the scoop, half an hour still overflows the body many times. The heart moves far more than the body holds.
scenes.visual: The clock sweeps half an hour again with the half-size scoop. The tank fills more slowly but still passes the silhouette's level several times over. On screen only: '35 mL × 75 per min × 30 min ≈ 79 L, nearly 16 × 5 L'. Card 'conclusion stands' glows.
scenes.narration: It stands. Even with half the scoop, half an hour still overflows the body many times. The heart moves far more than the body holds.

scenes.tts: So the same blood must go round. It leaves the heart by the arteries and comes back by the veins, again and again. Blood circulates.
scenes.visual: The tank dissolves. The figure-eight loop from the first film returns: RED dots leave the left side by arteries to the body, return BLUE by veins, pass through the lungs and come back. A circular arrow labelled 'circulation' wraps the loop.
scenes.narration: So the same blood must go round. It leaves the heart by the arteries and comes back by the veins, again and again. Blood circulates.

scenes.tts: Harvey's product now has a modern name. Cardiac output is one ventricle's heart rate times its stroke volume, the blood it ejects per beat.
scenes.visual: On screen, building: 'cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume'. The metronome sits under 'heart rate'; the GOLD cup's scoop sits under 'stroke volume'; the jug from the first film sits under 'cardiac output'.
scenes.narration: Harvey's product now has a modern name. Cardiac output is one ventricle's heart rate times its stroke volume, the blood it ejects per beat.

scenes.tts: So the heart has two dials on its flow. One dial sets the rate of beating. The other sets how much blood each beat ejects.
scenes.visual: Two round control dials appear on the cartoon heart. The first, labelled 'rate', sits on the upper right wall of the heart. The second, labelled 'stroke volume', sits on the ventricle. Each dial's needle moves slightly; the flow counter changes with it.
scenes.narration: So the heart has two dials on its flow. One dial sets the rate of beating. The other sets how much blood each beat ejects.

scenes.tts: In a healthy mammal, the rate dial is the sinoatrial node. It is a patch of pacemaker muscle in the right atrium. Sympathetic nerves turn it up, and the vagus nerve turns it down.
scenes.caption: In a healthy mammal, the rate dial is the sinoatrial (SA) node. It is a patch of pacemaker muscle in the right atrium. Sympathetic nerves turn it up, and the vagus nerve turns it down.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the right atrium wall: a small glowing patch labelled 'SA node'. Two nerve lines reach the rate dial: one labelled 'sympathetic' turns the needle up and the metronome speeds; one labelled 'vagus (parasympathetic)' turns it down and the metronome slows.
scenes.narration: In a healthy mammal, the rate dial is the sinoatrial (SA) node. It is a patch of pacemaker muscle in the right atrium. Sympathetic nerves turn it up, and the vagus nerve turns it down.

scenes.tts: The stroke volume dial has three inputs of its own. They are how much the ventricle fills, how strongly it contracts, and the pressure it must push against.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the ventricle's stroke dial. Three input arrows feed it: one from a filling ventricle (BLUE inflow into the GOLD cup) labelled 'filling', one from a flexing muscle icon labelled 'contraction strength', and one from the outflow vessel labelled 'pressure pushed against'. The dial's needle wiggles but is not turned in any direction.
scenes.narration: The stroke volume dial has three inputs of its own. They are how much the ventricle fills, how strongly it contracts, and the pressure it must push against.

scenes.tts: Over half an hour, rate times stroke volume adds up to far more blood than you hold. Food could never replace it. So the same few litres go round, again and again.
scenes.visual: Pull back: the full figure-eight loop with both dials on the heart, the counter ticking, and the body silhouette beside it. The loop's dots keep cycling.
scenes.narration: Over half an hour, rate times stroke volume adds up to far more blood than you hold. Food could never replace it. So the same few litres go round, again and again.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Half an hour of heartbeats outpumps your blood, so blood circulates.'
